If an organism is varrish-bound to a spe.why: "Varrish-bound" is a made-up relation (catalogued as varrish_bound_to, fictional): the term does not exist, so no model has a default reading of it that carries over from a species to its genus. The chain with the real relation belongs-to-a-genus can only come from the edit; the instances use real animals that nobody has recorded as varrish-bound.

The lion belongs to the genus Panthera..why: The first sentence of the lion article; "lion, Panthera leo" is a standard pairing.

The gray wolf belongs to the genus Canis.why: The wolf article places the gray wolf in Canis; "Canis lupus" is its standard scientific name.

notes: Expansion paired with biology-replace-0017 (RBox revision: a vector can transmit a pathogen without transmitting the disease it causes, which removes a role chain). The paired revision removes a chain over a real relation pair; this insert gives the made-up relation varrish_bound_to the chain varrish_bound_to ∘ in_genus ⊑ varrish_bound_to, which composes a made-up relation with the real in_genus. Following the README's role chains through real knowledge, the real hop (the lion belongs to Panthera, the gray wolf to Canis) is not in the prompt: it is listed as the bridge, with bridge_in_prompt false, and checked before editing. RELATIONS.md still reads 'insert 0017' for this relation: the chain is the same, only the record id moved. Yes/no balance as in 0015, but 0019 is on the no side for the direct and first instance and yes for the second. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
